ASTRA SECOND PRIVATE RESEARCH RECORD
Counting-space consequences and algebraic-logarithm bounds
Research date: 8 October 2026 UTC / 9 October 2026 Australia/Brisbane

PURPOSE AND STATUS

This is a compact, private scientific record of two completed research
outcomes, their independent mathematical reconstructions and comparisons,
original test code, and test results. It is an additional record, not a
replacement for either earlier archive. No public posting or external review
is represented by its creation.

The proof reconstructions and adversarial comparisons found no remaining
mathematical gap in the stated new bridges. This is an audited research proof
record, not a formal verification, outside specialist certification, peer-
reviewed publication, or established historical-priority claim. The conclusions
retain the supplied mathematical inputs explicitly identified below.

Only original scientific derivations, literature comparisons, audits, code,
results, and packaging/provenance information are included. Downloaded papers,
repository source copies, private routing material, and correspondence are not
included. Primary source links and immutable revisions are in EVIDENCE_PINS.txt.

OUTCOME 1: PRECISELY SCOPED COUNTING-SPACE NONCAPTURE

Define CPS(Card) locally to mean the deterministic, fixed finite-signature,
finite-support ASM formalism of Ferrarotti--Schewe, arXiv:2401.16366v1, extended
by ordinary BGS cardinality: Card(a) is the von Neumann ordinal |a| for a set,
and Empty for an atom. It includes no choice, powerset, succinct-number oracle,
or other unlisted primitive. FS24 itself omits Card and does not formally define
the counting extension asked about in its conclusion.

The new bridge: for each fixed such ASM M, one fixed Card-enabled HF term
program simulates its finite runs and halt/output behavior using at most
C_M W^(d_M) peak inclusive hereditary space, where
W = 4 + max_i |Active(S_i)|.
The bound is independent of the finite runtime. Fixed-arity nonzero function
graphs encode current states; updates preserve exact defaults, simultaneous
execution, duplicate handling, whole-state clash behavior, and zero deletion.
The compiler does not retain a history or unbounded step counter. Fixed-term
footprint accounting also covers temporary values and update sets.
